brewing.notes: A safe starting point for green tea: cooler water, short steeps, then adjust by taste.

description:
A jasmine-scented green tea from Xinjin in Chengdu, Sichuan, also known by the elegant name Bi Tan Piao Xue, 'snow drifting on a green pool'.

Treat it as you would any green tea: cooler water, short steeps, and a seller who can say where and when it was picked.
history: It is credited to Xu Jinhua, a cultural figure from Xinjin. Little more is documented about its background.
processing: Tender green buds picked before Qingming are scented by hand with jasmine blossoms gathered in the hot midsummer days.
harvest_season: Buds picked before Qingming; jasmine from high summer.
appearance_dry: Green leaf whose shape depends on the maker, as is usual for regional green teas.
appearance_liquor: Clear green, with pale blossoms floating on the surface.
appearance_wet: Usually soft green leaf that opens up in the water.
taste_profile: Green tea freshness carried by a strong jasmine fragrance.
vintage_note: Green teas like this are normally sold as the current year's harvest and are best within a year of picking. It is not an ageing tea.
